functions: Grossed-up taxable value of type 1 or type 2 fringe benefits at the 47% FBT rate

/*  FUNCTION NAME:  FBTGrossUpλ
    DESCRIPTION:*//**Grossed-up taxable value of type 1 or type 2 fringe benefits, FBTAA s 5B, at the 47% FBT rate and 10% GST rate, unrounded*/
/*  SOURCE:         Fringe Benefits Tax Assessment Act 1986, compilation 97 (1 July 2026), read 22 November 2026:
                    https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A03280/2026-07-01/2026-07-01/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html
                    s 5B(1B): type 1 aggregate fringe benefits amount x (FBT rate + GST rate) /
                    ((1 - FBT rate) x (1 + GST rate) x FBT rate). s 5B(1C): type 2 aggregate fringe
                    benefits amount x 1 / (1 - FBT rate). s 5B(3): the GST rate is the rate payable under
                    the GST Act, 10% (A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999 s 9-70).
                    Fringe Benefits Tax Act 1986, compilation 9 (19 June 2018), read 22 November 2026: s 6
                    sets the FBT rate at 47%; s 6A added 2 points for the years starting 1 April 2015 and
                    1 April 2016 only:
                    https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A03281/2018-06-19/2018-06-19/text/1/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html
                    ATO, 'Fringe benefits tax - rates and thresholds', last updated 20 May 2026, read 22 November
                    2026: 47%, type 1 2.0802 and type 2 1.8868 for the years ending 31 March 2023 to 2027,
                    which are these formulas to 4 decimal places:
                    https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/fringe-benefits-tax-rates-and-thresholds
*/
FBTGrossUpλ = LAMBDA(
//  Parameter Declaration
    [TaxableValues],
    [Type],
    LET(
    //  Help
        Help,           TRIM(TEXTSPLIT(
                            "FUNCTION:      →FBTGrossUpλ(TaxableValues, Type)¶" &
                            "DESCRIPTION:   →Grossed-up taxable value of type 1 or type 2 fringe benefits, FBTAA s 5B.¶NOTES!         →Grossed-up taxable value of fringe benefits under FBTAA s 5B: a type 1¶               →value (the employer can claim a GST credit for the benefit) times (47% +¶               →10%) / ((1 - 47%) x (1 + 10%) x 47%), a type 2 value times 1 / (1 - 47%).¶               →Those are the statute's factors, 2.08021... and 1.88679...; the ATO¶               →publishes them to 4 places as 2.0802 and 1.8868, so a figure from those¶               →differs by at most 0.01%. The type 2 factor also grosses up a reportable¶               →fringe benefits amount (s 135P). For FBT years from 1 April 2017 on, at¶               →47%; the years starting 1 April 2015 and 2016 used 49%. The result is not¶               →rounded. Rates only: it does not value a benefit, decide its type, or apply¶               →exemptions, the $30,000 or $17,000 caps or rebates.¶" &
                            "WEBPAGE:       →https://github.com/ryanduguid/Ozzit/blob/main/docs/australian-modelling.md¶" &
                            "VERSION:       →22 Nov 2026¶" &
                            "PARAMETERS:    →¶" &
                            "TaxableValues  →(Required) One or more taxable values, each 0 or more and under 10,000,000,000,000. A blank stays blank.¶" &
                            "Type           →(Required) 1 for a type 1 benefit, which carries a GST credit, or 2 for type 2: one for every value, or one for each.¶" &
                            "EXAMPLES:      →¶" &
                            "→Formula (oz is assumed to be the module's name)¶" &
                            "→=oz.FBTGrossUpλ({16500;6000}, {1;2})¶" &
                            "→Result¶" &
                            "→34323.5648¶" &
                            "→11320.7547",
                            "→", "¶"
                        )),
    //  Check inputs - Omitted required arguments
        Help?,          OR( ISOMITTED( TaxableValues), ISOMITTED( Type)),
    //  One type for every value, or one for each in the same shape
        OneType?,       AND( ROWS( Type) = 1, COLUMNS( Type) = 1),
        ValidShape?,    OR( OneType?, AND( ROWS( Type) = ROWS( TaxableValues), COLUMNS( Type) = COLUMNS( TaxableValues))),
        ShapeMessage,   "Type must be one type, or a type for each taxable value in the same shape.",
    //  A blank is nil and stays blank; an error passes so it shows
        ValidValue?,    AND( IF( ISERROR( TaxableValues), TRUE, IF( ISNUMBER( TaxableValues), ( TaxableValues >= 0) * ( TaxableValues < 1E13), TaxableValues & "" = ""))),
        ValueMessage,   "FBTGrossUpλ needs each taxable value to be a number from 0 to under 10,000,000,000,000, or blank.",
        Types,          IF( OneType?, IF( SEQUENCE( ROWS( TaxableValues), COLUMNS( TaxableValues)), Type), Type),
    //  A type is needed only beside a value; an error passes so it shows
        ValidType?,     IFERROR( AND( IF( ISERROR( TaxableValues), TRUE, IF( TaxableValues & "" = "", TRUE, IF( ISERROR( Types), TRUE, IF( ISNUMBER( Types), ( Types = 1) + ( Types = 2), FALSE))))), FALSE),
        TypeMessage,    "Type must be 1 or 2 for each taxable value.",
    //  Procedure - s 5B(1B) and (1C) at the 47% FBT rate and 10% GST rate
        FBT,            0.47,
        GST,            0.1,
        Result,         MAP( TaxableValues, Types, LAMBDA( Value, Kind,
                            IF( Value & "" = "", "", IF( Kind = 1, Value * ( FBT + GST) / (( 1 - FBT) * ( 1 + GST) * FBT), Value / ( 1 - FBT)))
                        )),
    //  Return Result, Help, or the message
        Return,         IF( Help?, 2, IF( NOT( ValidShape?), 3, IF( NOT( ValidValue?), 4, IF( NOT( ValidType?), 5, 1)))),
        CHOOSE( Return, Result, Help, ShapeMessage, ValueMessage, TypeMessage)
    )
);
